title: Third Punic War (149–146 BCE)
key_facts: Final Roman war against Carthage culminating in the siege and destruction of the city
Triggered by escalating Roman demands and fears of Carthaginian revival
Resulted in Carthage’s annihilation and annexation as the province of Africa
causes: Roman suspicion of Carthage despite earlier treaties
Carthage’s self-defense against Numidia used as pretext by Rome
outcome: City of Carthage destroyed (146 BCE); survivors enslaved
Territory reorganized as the Roman province of Africa
impacts: Eliminated Rome’s chief rival in the western Mediterranean
